entities.label: PETITIONER

sentences.text: Mr. Mrityunjoy Chatterjee, Mr. V. N. Jhaa, Mr. S. Ganguly, Mr. A. Sarkar, ... for the petitioner.

The present revisional application has been preferred praying for quashing of the proceedings in Gr
Case No. 664 of 2024 vide Complaint Case No. 1900 of 2023 in Ashoknagar Police Station Case No.
161 of 2024 dated 15.03.2024 under Sections 420/406/409 of the Indian Penal Code, pending
before the learned Court of Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate, Barasat.

entities.text: Court of Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate, Barasat
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The proceeding in the present case has been initiated on an application under Section 156(3) of the Cr. P. C. from wherein it appears that the complainant and the accused were in a business relationship.
The business between the parties started in the year 2021 and since then there has been supply of goods by the complainant and payment received from the accused.
It is alleged that subsequently the accused person defaulted in payment of certain amount which is due to the complainant.

It further appears that a cheque issued by the accused was allegedly dishonoured and as such the present case has been initiated.
From the contents of the application under Section 156(3) of the Cr. P. C. it prima facie appears that there was no deception in the initial period of business transaction and the relief for cheque being dishonoured lies before a different forum.
Considering the said facts, the petitioner has made out an arguable case

and as such the proceedings in GR Case No. 664 of 2024 vide Complaint Case No. 1900 of 2023 in Ashoknagar Police Station Case No. 161 of 2024 dated 15.03.2024 under Sections 420/406/409 of the Indian Penal Code,
pending before the learned Court of Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate, Barasat, be stayed till 28th July, 2025 or until further orders, whichever is earlier.
